script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Saying nobody in the scene is skipping a meal adds a detail the text does not give.
The quoted imagined line puts a joke paraphrase in the disciple's mouth.
The joke about carrying a week's bread uses a food other than cookies in a joke, rather than mentioning it as a Bible fact.
The pantry joke uses a year's supply of bread as an imagined scenario, rather than mentioning bread as a Bible fact.
The story does not say the man knocks at his friend's door.
The text does not say the friend never opens the door.
Saying the friend wants to stay put assigns him a feeling the text does not give.
The text says the man gets as much as he needs; it does not specify the number of loaves he receives.
Saying nothing is cut in half adds a detail the story does not give.
The midnight story does not say the man stood knocking at a door.
The story does not say the man was standing at the door.
The passage does not say the listeners are in a room.
The dinner joke uses the fish from the passage in an imagined food joke, rather than mentioning it as a Bible fact.
The explanation turns 'how much more will your Father ... give the Holy Spirit' into a claim that the Father gives a greater quantity. The verse names the Holy Spirit as the gift.
